name: Château des Vigiers
architectural_style: A 16th-century château at the heart of the Périgord-Dordogne vineyards, paired since 1993 with a modern golf-resort wing designed around an 18-hole (now 27-hole) course by architect Donald Steel
accessibility: 65 rooms are split between the 16th-century château and the modern Relais building beside the golf course; contact the hotel directly regarding specific accessibility requirements.
tagline: A 1597 Périgord château paired with one of southwest France's top-10 golf courses, its 65 rooms mostly in a modern wing beside the first tee
highlights: The château dates to 1597, at the heart of the Périgord-Dordogne vineyards
Golf architect Donald Steel designed the 18-hole course, opened in March 1992; the resort now has 27 holes, ranked among the top 10 in southwest France
The château itself became a four-star, 25-room hotel in May 1993
description:
Château des Vigiers dates to 1597, at the heart of the Périgord-Dordogne vineyards in southwest France. Golf course architect Donald Steel designed the 18-hole course, opened in March 1992, and the château was transformed into a four-star hotel with 25 rooms, opening its doors in May 1993. Today the resort has a 27-hole course (three possible 18-hole combinations), ranked among the top 10 in southwest France.

Today its 65 rooms are split between two buildings: the Château (25 rooms, 16th-century right wing of the historic building, overlooking the courtyard or the golf course) and the Relais (40 rooms, a modern building beside the first tee).

The pairing of a 1597 château with a purpose-built, Donald Steel-designed golf resort gives Vigiers a distinctly different character from the more purely historic château-hotels found elsewhere in the France collection.

The fact that most of the room inventory (40 of 65) sits in the modern Relais building, rather than the historic château, means most guests here are choosing the resort and golf experience rather than a period-accurate château stay.

The château's restaurant, Les Fresques, held a Michelin star from 2014 to 2017, giving the property a documented high-end culinary pedigree inside the historic building itself.

The estate's position 30 minutes from Bergerac airport and about 1h30 from Bordeaux gives guests staying at Vigiers convenient access to both the wider Dordogne wine country and Saint-Émilion.

faqs.question: Are most of the rooms at Château des Vigiers inside the historic building?
faqs.answer: No — only 25 of the 65 rooms are in the 16th-century château itself; the remaining 40 are in the modern Relais building beside the golf course. Guests wanting the château specifically should book that category.

faqs.question: What is the golf course at Château des Vigiers known for?
faqs.answer: Designed by architect Donald Steel and opened in 1992, it has since expanded to 27 holes and ranks among the top 10 courses in southwest France.

faqs.question: Did Château des Vigiers ever hold a Michelin star?
faqs.answer: Yes — its restaurant, Les Fresques, held a Michelin star from 2014 to 2017.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** 30 minutes from Bergerac airport, about 1h30 from Bordeaux, at the heart of the Périgord-Dordogne wine country.

**Rooms & rates:** 65 rooms split between the 16th-century château (25 rooms) and the Relais, a modern building beside the golf course (40 rooms); from about €156 per night.

**On-site:** A 27-hole golf course, among the top 10 in southwest France; Les Fresques restaurant in the château itself (Michelin star 2014-2017); spa.

**Good to know:** Only 25 of the 65 rooms are in the 16th-century building — most of the inventory is in the Relais, a modern building beside the golf course; guests wanting the château specifically should book that category.

**Combine with:** Bergerac (30 min), Saint-Émilion (1h).
